works.name: Baluarte da Ribeira (Forte do Terreiro do Paço)

past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 49% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
7 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
A great fire burned 17 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The duke planted a “New Town” across the river: one straight street of equal plots. It never prospered on its own, and the council bought it out a generation later.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 85% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 49 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the northern side; 28 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.

places.name: Cacilhas
past: An older settlement grew into a town in Roman times. Its main routes survive, with irregular medieval lanes and plots shaped by the ground.
3 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled, the river and the lie of the land sparing a stretch of the circuit.
The Franciscans were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 20 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Alcântara
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The ford was bridged in stone.
The duke planted a “New Town” across the river: one straight street of equal plots. It never prospered on its own, and the council bought it out a generation later.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 73% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 9 houses were built into what was left of it.
A great fire burned 22 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 16 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Campolide
past: Settled on the riverbank for the water and the fishing.
Walled, the river and the lie of the land sparing a stretch of the circuit.
A great fire burned 15 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The Carmelites were given ground by the wall for their friary.
A great fire burned 20 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 70 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the eastern side; 18 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 8 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
